We need to produce correct answer. Better to actually call apply_template to get precise precursors. Let's attempt to construct product SMILES without mapping. Use the right side string: '[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20])[O:21]1'

Remove mapping numbers and brackets but keep stereochemistry: Replace [CH3] with C, [CH2] with C, [O] with O, [C] with C, [C@H] with C@H, [C@@H] with C@@H, [CH] with C, etc. Also need to keep parentheses.

Thus product SMILES: 'CCO C(=O)C[C@H]1CC[C@H](O)C(C)(C@@H)(/C=C(C)C(=O)OC)O1' Wait there is a slash for stereochemistry.

Let's construct:

Start: CH3-CH2-O-C(=O)-CH2- C@H1-CH2- C@H(OH)- C@@H(CH3)- C@@H( /CH= C( /CH3 ) C(=O) OCH3 ) O1

So SMILES: 'CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CC[C@H](O)C(C)(C@@H)(/C=C(C)C(=O)OC)O1' but need correct placement of CH3 on C@@H earlier: C@@H(CH3) is a methyl substituent on that carbon, which is already part of ring? Actually C@@H is part of ring, with a methyl substituent. So ring carbon has methyl and the side chain.

Thus ring carbon is C@@H(C)(/C=C(C)C(=O)OC). So SMILES: 'CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CC[C@H](O)C(C)(C@@H)(/C=C(C)C(=O)OC)O1' Not correct.

Better to just use apply_template tool to get precursors directly, providing product SMILES as above. Let's attempt with product SMILES guess and see if tool returns something.
